questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture, the weather, the duration of the study period.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, calling KU helped a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance from my home university, but my host university helped clarify some things about my stay there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: My host university, especially the teachers, thought we as exchange students knew more than what we actually did, but it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very luck to find housing through people that had been there the year before. For Australia, I think get there and then find housing when you are there is what I have heard.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would prefer to live off campus, because it is much easier to explore the city that way, but it also depends on where the campus is located. If it is in the middle of the city it might be fine. I have heard the rooms are small and expensive, so I would try to find something elsewhere.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You go on to there website and then fill out a form and send it in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call or email them

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fairly succesful, it all depends on how you want your schedule to look like. You could also register for a course just to be sure and then change your mind later on.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register early on if you want to be sure, and then change the courses if you later find out that you have changed your mind. It is quite easy to change the courses and the day/time of day you have your courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think due to the university's structure and grading system, it was much easier than UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The exam does not count 100%, you have multiple things counting towards your grade throughout the semester. The teaching differed a lot from course to course. I think the teaching was not as good as at UCPH, but still fine.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Applied Statistics, Statistical Inference, Linear Models, Investments

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Statistical Inference. Fun course if you enjoy the theoretical part of statistics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent more on transport than expected but else I did not encounter unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think just living in general is more expensive when on exchange because you want to travel and do many activities with your friends.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could join many different sports teams and many different clubs. You could do a global leadership program as well

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you live close to campus I think joining a sportsteam would be fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on as many weekend trips as possible and travel when you have student vacation. There are many great hikes in and around Sydney.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. They all speak english of course and the culture is much like our own.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in the breaks or before the lecture starts

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: All of my teachers were from Asia and most had a very thick accent, that was probably the most challenging, because it could be hard to understand. Otherwise there were no cultural differences that were challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly they are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open minded, mingle with exchange students from other countries and explore the city.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: MQ is a bit far from the city, but it is super easy to get there with the new metro line, but I would not recommend living on campus. Try to plan you schedule such that you have all your classes in a few days as possible.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to see new parts of the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from everything back home, but it goes by very quickly, so it is alright.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
